question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> mole of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>PbS</mi></math> is oxidised by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> moles of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> to get <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></math> moles of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>.</mo></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mo>=</mo></math>

solution.text:
Given that, 1 mole of PbS is oxidised by X moles of O3 to get Y moles of O2.

The balanced chemical equation can be written as,

PbS+4O3→PbSO4+4O2

Here x = 4, y = 4 

Hence,

 X+Y=4+4=8
